title: vaccinium uliginosum subsp. occidentale
intro: Vaccinium uliginosum subsp. occidentale, commonly known as Western Bog Bilberry, is a subspecies of the Vaccinium uliginosum plant, a type of low-growing shrub that produces small, blue-purple berries. The berries of the Western Bog Bilberry are rich in antioxidants and have been traditionally used in folk medicine to support digestive health and boost the immune system. The therapeutic actions of Western Bog Bilberry berries include anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which may help to reduce inflammation and prevent infections. The berries contain bioactive constituents such as anthocyanins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.
